text: A finite size object is placed normal to the principal axis at a distance of 30 cm from a convex mirror of focal length 30 cm . A plane mirror is now placed in such a way that the image produced by both the mirrors coincide with each other. The distance between the two mirrors is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the convex mirror: $u=-30\text{cm}$, $f=+30\text{cm}$.

$\frac{1}{v}=\frac{1}{f}-\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{30}+\frac{1}{30}=\frac{1}{15}\Rightarrow v=+15\text{cm}$

The image is virtual, 15 cm behind the convex mirror, so it lies $30+15=45\text{cm}$ from the object.


[IMG]

A plane mirror forms the image as far behind it as the object is in front of it. For its image to fall at the same point, the plane mirror must face the object midway between the object and that image, i.e. $\dfrac{45}{2}=22.5\text{cm}$ from the object.

Distance between the two mirrors $=30-22.5=7.5\text{cm}$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text:
Displacement of a wave is expressed as $x(t)=5\cos \left (628t+\frac{π}{2}\right )\mathrm{m}$. The wavelength of the wave when its velocity is $300\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ is :

$(π=3.14)$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{x}(\mathrm{t})=5\cos \left [628\mathrm{t}+\dfrac{π}{2}\right ]\mathrm{m} \\ \text{velocity}(\mathrm{v}_{ω})=300\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s} \\ \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{w}}=\dfrac{ω}{\mathrm{K}} \\ 300=\dfrac{628}{\mathrm{K}}\Rightarrow \mathrm{K}=\dfrac{628}{300} \\ \dfrac{2π}{λ}=\dfrac{628}{300}\Rightarrow λ=\dfrac{2\times 3.14\times 300}{628} \\ λ=3\mathrm{m} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text:
A metallic ring is uniformly charged as shown in figure. AC and BD are two mutually perpendicular diameters. Electric field due to arc $AB$ at ' $O$ ' is ' $E$ ' in magnitude. What would be the magnitude of electric field at ' O ' due to arc ABC ?

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Take the charge on the ring as positive. By symmetry, the field at O due to the uniformly charged quarter arc AB has magnitude $E$ along the bisector of $\angle AOB$, pointing away from the arc.

Arc ABC consists of arc AB and arc BC. Arc BC is arc AB turned through $90^{\circ }$ about O, so its field at O also has magnitude $E$ and is at $90^{\circ }$ to the field of arc AB.

Resolving along the two diameters, the components along AC cancel and the components along BD add:

$E_{ABC}=2E\cos 45^{\circ }=\sqrt{2}E$

directed from B towards D.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: A wheel is rolling on a plane surface. The speed of a particle on the highest point of the rim is $8\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$. The speed of the particle on the rim of the wheel at the same level as the centre of wheel, will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In rolling without slipping, the contact point A is the instantaneous centre of rotation, so every point of the wheel moves with speed $ω$ times its distance from A.


[IMG]

The highest point B is at distance $2R$ from A, so $v_{B}=ω(2R)=2v$, where $v=ωR$ is the speed of the centre. With $v_{B}=8\text{m s}^{-1}$, $v=4\text{m s}^{-1}$.

The rim point P at the level of the centre is at distance $AP=\sqrt{R^{2}+R^{2}}=\sqrt{2}R$ from A:

$v_{P}=ω\sqrt{2}R=\sqrt{2}v=4\sqrt{2}\text{m s}^{-1}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text:
The displacement x versus time graph is shown below.


[IMG]


(A) The average velocity during 0 to 3 s is $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

(B) The average velocity during 3 to 5 s is $0\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

(C) The instantaneous velocity at $\mathrm{t}=2\mathrm{s}$ is $5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

(D) The average velocity during 5 to 7 s and instantaneous velocity at $\mathrm{t}=6.5\mathrm{s}$ are equal

(E) The average velocity from $t=0$ to $t=9\mathrm{s}$ is zero

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The graph is made of straight segments joining $(0,0)$, $(1,-5)$, $(2,0)$, $(3,5)$, $(5,5)$, $(6,10)$, $(7,0)$, $(8,-5)$ and $(9,0)$, with $t$ in s and $x$ in m.

(A) Average velocity from 0 to 3 s $=\dfrac{5-0}{3}=\dfrac{5}{3}\text{m s}^{-1}$, not $10\text{m s}^{-1}$: false.

(B) From 3 s to 5 s, $x$ stays at 5 m, so the average velocity $=\dfrac{5-5}{2}=0$: true.

(C) From 1 s to 3 s the graph is one straight line from $-5$ m to $5$ m, so the velocity at $t=2$ s is its slope $\dfrac{5-(-5)}{3-1}=5\text{m s}^{-1}$: true.

(D) Average velocity from 5 s to 7 s $=\dfrac{0-5}{2}=-2.5\text{m s}^{-1}$, while at $t=6.5$ s the velocity is the slope of the segment from $(6,10)$ to $(7,0)$, $\dfrac{0-10}{1}=-10\text{m s}^{-1}$; the two are unequal: false.

(E) $x=0$ at both $t=0$ and $t=9$ s, so the average velocity over this interval is zero: true.

The correct statements are (B), (C) and (E).

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: Consider a rectangular sheet of solid material of length $l=9\mathrm{cm}$ and width $\mathrm{d}=4\mathrm{cm}$. The coefficient of linear expansion is $α=3.1\times 10^{-5}\mathrm{K}^{-1}$ at room temperature and one atmospheric pressure. The mass of sheet $m=0.1\mathrm{kg}$ and the specific heat capacity $C_{\mathrm{v}}=900\mathrm{J}\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\mathrm{K}^{-1}$. If the amount of heat supplied to the material is $8.1\times 10^{2}\mathrm{J}$ then change in area of the rectangular sheet is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Calculate the Change in Temperature:

Use the formula:

$\Delta Q=mC_{v}\Delta T$

Given:

$\Delta Q=8.1\times 10^{2}\text{J}$

$m=0.1\text{kg}$

$C_{v}=900\text{J}\text{kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$

Substitute the values to find $\Delta T$:

$8.1\times 10^{2}=0.1\times 900\times \Delta T$

Solving for $\Delta T$:

$\Delta T=\frac{8.1\times 10^{2}}{0.1\times 900}=9\text{K}$

Calculate the Change in Area:

The change in area $\Delta A$ is calculated using:

$\Delta A=A_{0}\times 2α\Delta T$

Where:

$A_{0}$ is the original area of the sheet.

$α=3.1\times 10^{-5}\text{K}^{-1}$.

$\Delta T=9\text{K}$.

First, calculate the original area $A_{0}$:

$A_{0}=l\times d=9\text{cm}\times 4\text{cm}=36\text{cm}^{2}=0.0036\text{m}^{2}$

Now, substitute into the formula for $\Delta A$:

$\Delta A=0.0036\times 2\times 3.1\times 10^{-5}\times 9$

Simplifying:

$\Delta A=2.0\times 10^{-6}\text{m}^{2}$

Therefore, the change in area of the rectangular sheet is $2.0\times 10^{-6}\text{m}^{2}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: For the determination of refractive index of glass slab, a travelling microscope is used whose main scale contains 300 equal divisions equals to 15 cm . The vernier scale attached to the microscope has 25 divisions equals to 24 divisions of main scale. The least count (LC) of the travelling microscope is (in cm ) :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Determine one main scale division (msd):

$300\text{msd}=15\text{cm}$

Therefore,

$1~\text{msd}=\frac{15}{300}\text{cm}=0.05\text{cm}$

Determine one vernier scale division (vsd):

$25\quad \text{vsd}=24\text{msd}$

Therefore,

$1~\text{vsd}=\frac{24}{25}\text{msd}$

Calculate the least count (LC):

The least count is given by the difference between one main scale division and one vernier scale division:

$\text{LC}=1\text{msd}-1\text{vsd}$

Substitute the expression for 1 vsd:

$\text{LC}=1\text{msd}-\frac{24}{25}\times 1\text{msd}$

This simplifies to:

$\text{LC}=\frac{1}{25}\times 1\text{msd}$

Calculate the LC in cm:

Substituting the value of 1 msd:

$\text{LC}=\frac{1}{25}\times 0.05\text{cm}=0.002\text{cm}$

Hence, the least count of the traveling microscope is 0.002 cm.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text:
Three parallel plate capacitors $C_{1},C_{2}$ and $C_{3}$ each of capacitance $5μ\mathrm{F}$ are connected as shown in figure. The effective capacitance between points $A$ and $B$, when the space between the parallel plates of $C_{1}$ capacitor is filled with a dielectric medium having dielectric constant of 4, is :


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Update Capacitance of $C_{1}$:

The initial capacitance of $C_{1}$ is $5~μ\text{F}$. Adding a dielectric with a dielectric constant of 4 increases $C_{1}$ to:

$C_{1}=4\times 5=20μ\text{F}$

Identify Capacitances of $C_{2}$ and $C_{3}$:

Both $C_{2}$ and $C_{3}$ remain at $5~μ\text{F}$ since no dielectric is added to them.

$C_{2}=5μ\text{F},C_{3}=5μ\text{F}$

Calculate Effective Capacitance:

Capacitors $C_{1}$ and $C_{2}$ are in series, and this series combination is parallel to $C_{3}$.

Series Combination of $C_{1}$ and $C_{2}$:

The formula for capacitors in series is:

$C_{\text{series}}=\frac{C_{1}\times C_{2}}{C_{1}+C_{2}}=\frac{20\times 5}{20+5}=\frac{100}{25}=4μ\text{F}$

Parallel Combination with $C_{3}$:

The formula for capacitors in parallel is:

$C_{\text{eq}}=C_{\text{series}}+C_{3}=4+5=9μ\text{F}$

Thus, the effective capacitance between points $A$ and $B$ is $9~μ\text{F}$.

text: There are ' $n$ ' number of identical electric bulbs, each is designed to draw a power $p$ independently from the mains supply. They are now joined in series across the mains supply. The total power drawn by the combination is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Each bulb draws power $p$ when connected alone across the mains of voltage $V$, so the resistance of each bulb is

$R=\dfrac{V^{2}}{p}$

The resistance of a bulb does not change, so $n$ such bulbs in series have total resistance

$R_{s}=nR=\dfrac{nV^{2}}{p}$

The combination is connected across the same mains voltage $V$, so the total power drawn is

$P_{s}=\dfrac{V^{2}}{R_{s}}=\dfrac{V^{2}}{nV^{2}/p}=\dfrac{p}{n}$

The common series current is $I=\dfrac{V}{nR}$, $n$ times smaller than the current of one bulb alone, so $P_{s}=I^{2}(nR)$ also gives $\dfrac{p}{n}$, not $np$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text:
Consider a n-type semiconductor in which $\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{e}}$ and $\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{h}}$ are number of electrons and holes, respectively.

(A) Holes are minority carriers

(B) The dopant is a pentavalent atom

(C) $\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{e}}\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{h}}\neq \mathrm{n}_{i}^{2}$

(where $\mathrm{n}_{i}$ is number of electrons or holes in semiconductor when it is intrinsic form)

(D) $\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{e}}\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{h}}⩾\mathrm{n}_{i}^{2}$

(E) The holes are not generated due to the donors

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In an n-type semiconductor the dopant is a pentavalent atom (P, As, Sb): four of its valence electrons form covalent bonds and the fifth is donated to the conduction band, so (B) is correct.

These donated electrons make electrons the majority carriers and holes the minority carriers, so (A) is correct.

A donor atom gives up an electron without creating a hole in the valence band; holes arise only from thermal generation of electron-hole pairs, so (E) is correct.

In thermal equilibrium the law of mass action $n_{e}n_{h}=n_{i}^{2}$ holds for an extrinsic semiconductor as well as an intrinsic one, so (C) $n_{e}n_{h}\neq n_{i}^{2}$ is wrong; (D) is also rejected, because the product stays fixed at $n_{i}^{2}$ and never exceeds it.

The correct statements are (A), (B) and (E).

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: A solid sphere with uniform density and radius $R$ is rotating initially with constant angular velocity $(ω_{1})$ about its diameter. After some time during the rotation it starts losing mass at a uniform rate, with no change in its shape. The angular velocity of the sphere when its radius become $\mathrm{R}/2$ is $xω_{1}$. The value of $x$ is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When sphere is of radius $R$, its mass is $M$, when radius is reduced to $\frac{R}{2}$, mass will reduced to $\frac{M}{8}$

Now by conservation of angular momentum

$\begin{array}{l} (τ_{\mathrm{ext}}=0) \\ \mathrm{L}_{1}=\mathrm{L}_{2} \\ \mathrm{I}_{1}ω_{1}=\mathrm{I}_{2}ω_{2} \\ \left (\dfrac{2}{5}\mathrm{MR}^{2}\right )ω_{1}=\left (\dfrac{2}{5}\left (\dfrac{\mathrm{M}}{8}\right )\left (\dfrac{\mathrm{R}}{2}\right )^{2}\right )ω_{2} \end{array}$

$ω_{2}=32ω_{1}$ value of x is 32

Answer is 32
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: An inductor of self inductance 1 H is connected in series with a resistor of $100π$ ohm and an ac supply of $100π$ volt, 50 Hz . Maximum current flowing in the circuit is $_________ A$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Impedance of circuit

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{Z}=\sqrt{\mathrm{R}^{2}+(\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}})^{2}}=\sqrt{\mathrm{R}^{2}+(ω\mathrm{L})^{2}} \\ =\sqrt{(100π)^{2}+(2π\times 50\times 1)^{2}} \\ =\sqrt{(100π)^{2}+(100π)^{2}} \\ =\sqrt{2}\times 100π \\ \mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{rms}}=\dfrac{\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{Z}}=\dfrac{100π}{\sqrt{2}\times 100π}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \mathrm{I}_{\max }=\sqrt{2}\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{rms}}=\sqrt{2}\times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=1\text{Ampere} \end{array}$

Correct Answer : 1
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text:
If an optical medium possesses a relative permeability of $\frac{10}{π}$ and relative permittivity of $\frac{1}{0.0885}$, then the velocity of light is greater in vacuum than that in this medium by $_________$ times.

$\left (μ_{0}=4π\times 10^{-7}\mathrm{H}/\mathrm{m},𝜖_{0}=8.85\times 10^{-12}\mathrm{F}/\mathrm{m},\mathrm{c}=3\times 10^{8}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}\right )$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \text{Since velocity of light in terms of}μ&E\text{is} \\ \begin{array}{l} V=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{μ𝜖}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{μ_{0}μ_{\mathrm{r}}}}\times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{𝜖_{0}𝜖_{\mathrm{r}}}} \\ =\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{μ_{\mathrm{r}}𝜖_{\mathrm{r}}}}\times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{μ_{0}𝜖_{0}}} \\ =\dfrac{C}{\sqrt{μ_{\mathrm{r}}𝜖_{\mathrm{r}}}}=\dfrac{C}{\sqrt{\frac{10}{π}\times \frac{1}{0.0885}}} \\ =\dfrac{C}{\sqrt{36}}=\dfrac{C}{6} \end{array} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{ll} V & =\dfrac{C}{6} \\ C & =6V \end{array}$

Velocity of light in vacuum is greater by 6 times the velocity of light in medium
Answer is 6

text: A particle of charge $1.6μ\mathrm{C}$ and mass $16μ\mathrm{g}$ is present in a strong magnetic field of 6.28 T . The particle is then fired perpendicular to magnetic field. The time required for the particle to return to original location for the first time is $_________ s$. $(π=3.14)$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a charged particle moving perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field, it performs uniform circular motion.

The time taken to return to the original position for the first time is the time period of circular motion:

$T=\frac{2πm}{qB}$

Now substitute the given values.

Given:
$q=1.6μC=1.6\times 10^{-6}C$

$m=16μg=16\times 10^{-9}kg$

because

$1μg=10^{-9}kg$

and

$B=6.28T$

Using

$T=\frac{2πm}{qB}$

$T=\frac{2\times 3.14\times 16\times 10^{-9}}{1.6\times 10^{-6}\times 6.28}$

Now simplify:

Since

$2\times 3.14=6.28$

$T=\frac{6.28\times 16\times 10^{-9}}{1.6\times 10^{-6}\times 6.28}$

Cancel $6.28$ from numerator and denominator:

$T=\frac{16\times 10^{-9}}{1.6\times 10^{-6}}$

$T=\frac{16}{1.6}\times 10^{-3}$

$T=10\times 10^{-3}$

$T=10^{-2}s$

So, the required time is

$0.01\text{s}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: In a Young's double slit experiment, two slits are located 1.5 mm apart. The distance of screen from slits is 2 m and the wavelength of the source is 400 nm . If the 20 maxima of the double slit pattern are contained within the central maximum of the single slit diffraction pattern, then the width of each slit is $x\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{cm}$, where $x$-value is $_________$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Width of 20 maxima of double slit $=$ width of central maxima of single slit

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{20λ\mathrm{D}}{\mathrm{d}}=\dfrac{2λ\mathrm{D}}{\mathrm{a}} \\ \dfrac{10}{\mathrm{d}}=\dfrac{1}{\mathrm{a}} \\ \mathrm{a}=\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{10}=\dfrac{1.5\times 10^{-1}}{10}\mathrm{cm}=15\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{cm} \end{array}$

Value of $x$ is 15

Answer is 15
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift
